t: You're on the ground once occupied by St Michael Bassishaw, a parish church on Basinghall Street. The land is now taken up by the Barbican Centre. The church was recorded from the twelfth century and was destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666. It was rebuilt by the office of Sir Christopher Wren, then demolished in 1900. Buried here were two Lord Mayors of London, Sir John Gresham, who also founded Gresham's School, and Sir Wolstan Dixie. The Scottish cleric and mathematician William Braikenridge, a Fellow of the Royal Society, was buried here too.
